brief.subject: FTC targets imposter scams and health plan sales tricks
brief.headline: FTC Pulls 19 Fake FTC Sites as Imposter Scams Stay Top Fraud Complaint
brief.dek: The FTC reports imposter-scam crackdown results, warns health plan marketers during open enrollment, and sues Dollar General over register prices.
brief.lede: The FTC says imposter scams have been the top reported fraud category. It has removed 19 websites pretending to be the agency itself.

sections.heading: Imposter Scam Crackdown Results
bullets: The FTC took down 19 websites posing as the FTC, so official-looking pages can still be fake.
Enforcement under the Impersonation Rule has produced more than $80 million in consumer redress.
That rule took effect in 2024, giving regulators a sharper tool against people faking government or business identities.
Imposter scams lead reported fraud, according to the FTC, making them the threat most worth discussing with older relatives.

sections.heading: Open Enrollment Sales Warning
bullets: FTC staff sent warning letters to 25 companies that market or generate leads for healthcare plans.
The letters flag likely deceptive or unfair claims about plan terms during the current open enrollment season.
More letters are expected on a rolling basis, so be skeptical of plan pitches that sound unusually generous.

sections.heading: Shelf Price Versus Register Price
bullets: The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General over allegedly charging more at checkout than shelf tags and ads showed.
Regulators say the practice ran for years and cost shoppers millions of dollars.
Checking receipts against posted prices is a simple habit that can catch overcharges.

sections.heading: Your Data and the Price You Pay
bullets: The FTC ordered nine airlines, ride-sharing and food-delivery firms to explain how personal data shapes prices and gig pay.
The inquiry could reveal whether consumers are quietly charged different amounts based on their information.

brief.seo_description: FTC removes 19 fake FTC websites, warns 25 health plan marketers during open enrollment, and sues Dollar General with 20 states over pricing.
